question:
Prove that
$$\begin{vmatrix}a+b & b+c & c+a\\c & a & b\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}=a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca$$
Hence, evaluate the determinant when $a=5$, $b=2$, and $c=-1$.
explanation:
Applying column operations
Let
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}a+b & b+c & c+a\\c & a & b\\1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
Apply $C_1\to C_1-C_3$ and $C_2\to C_2-C_3$:
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}b-c & b-a & c+a\\c-b & a-b & b\\0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
Expanding along the third row,
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}b-c & b-a\\c-b & a-b\end{vmatrix}$$
$$D=(b-c)(a-b)-(b-a)(c-b)$$
Since $b-a=-(a-b)$ and $c-b=-(b-c)$,
$$D=(b-c)(a-b)-(a-b)(b-c)(-1)(-1)$$
Direct simplification of the products gives
$$D=ab-b^2-ac+bc-bc+b^2+ac-a^2$$
This simplification does not produce the required expression, so the determinant is evaluated directly to verify the stated relation.

Direct evaluation
Expanding the original determinant along the third row,
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}b+c & c+a\\a & b\end{vmatrix}-\begin{vmatrix}a+b & c+a\\c & b\end{vmatrix}+\begin{vmatrix}a+b & b+c\\c & a\end{vmatrix}$$
$$D=b(b+c)-a(c+a)-\left[b(a+b)-c(c+a)\right]+\left[a(a+b)-c(b+c)\right]$$
$$D=b^2+bc-ac-a^2-ab-b^2+c^2+ac+a^2+ab-bc-c^2=0$$
Thus, the proposed identity is not valid; the determinant is identically zero.

Substitution
For $a=5$, $b=2$, and $c=-1$, the determinant is therefore
$$D=0$$

options.A: The stated identity is valid, and the determinant equals $a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca$; for $a=5,b=2,c=-1$, its value is $27$
options.B: The stated identity is not valid; the determinant is identically $0$, and for $a=5,b=2,c=-1$, its value is $0$
options.C: The determinant equals $ab+bc+ca$; for $a=5,b=2,c=-1$, its value is $3$
options.D: The determinant equals $(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)$; for $a=5,b=2,c=-1$, its value is $54$
